chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

a man who became junub during the night of Ramadan, then deliberately omitted the ritual bath until dawn. He said: 'He must free a slave, or fast two consecutive months, or feed sixty poor people.' He said, and he said: 'He is worthy that I do not think he will ever catch up [with the missed obligation].'

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: became junub (ritually impure due to sexual intercourse or emission)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for deliberately delaying ghusl until dawn in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the *kaffarah* for deliberately delaying *ghusl* until dawn in Ramadan, prescribing freeing a slave, fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) adds a nuanced scholarly observation that the delay itself makes it unlikely the person will actually complete the expiation, highlighting the severity of the negligence. This ruling is often compared to the expiation for accidental intercourse during Ramadan, though here the focus is on the ritual impurity state persisting into the fasting time.
